verdict.proportion_verdict: Confirmation message ('Change saved.') and the inline Undo action are both set at the identical --type-body: 16px (index.html lines 21-23, 243, 261). verdict.one_line: A clean, token-disciplined dark snackbar where Undo is rightly same-sized as the message and differentiated only by weight/color — solid craft, minor low-severity nits only.
strengths: Full design-token discipline: every color/spacing/type/motion value in the component traces to a CSS custom property with a documented fallback, and undocumented additions (timer, radius, shadow) are explicitly flagged in comments as local extensions rather than silently invented

Accessible construction: aria-live='polite' region, role='status', 44x44px minimum tap targets on Undo/dismiss, Escape-to-dismiss, aria-label on the icon-only close button

refutation.note:
All three reported defects hold up on direct inspection of index.html. (1) Timer bar scope-creep confirmed verbatim — lines 49-52 and 316-329 literally comment 'local component tokens (not in DESIGN.md)' and 'not in DESIGN.md, defined here'; three added CSS custom properties plus a new DOM node (#snackbar-timer) beyond the brief's three named elements. (2) Contrast: I independently computed WCAG relative luminance for #ed4609 on #141414 and get ~4.72:1 (reviewer said ~4.81:1 — a small discrepancy, likely a rounding/formula difference, but the substantive conclusion — passes AA-normal-text 4.5:1 with very little headroom — holds either way). (3) Save-button no-state-change confirmed at lines 357/447-452: click handler calls setStatus() and openSnackbar() but never touches saveBtn's class, text, or disabled attribute, even though the adjacent status label visibly changes color/weight. All three are correctly low severity and don't threaten ship_ready.

One real defect the reviewer missed: the snackbar has a hard 5-second auto-dismiss (--snackbar-auto-dismiss-ms: 5000, line 51) with NO pause-on-hover/focus and no way to extend/disable it (verified in script: setTimeout at lines 430-434, no mouseenter/mouseleave/focus listeners anywhere in the file). This is a WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable) risk — a component whose entire raison d'être is giving the user a window to click Undo removes that window unconditionally after 5s regardless of user speed, assistive-tech dwell time, or whether their cursor is currently over the snackbar. This is a more substantive a11y gap than any of the three reported nits (I'd call it medium, not low) and should have been caught given how thorough the reviewer was on aria-live/role/focus-visible/tap-targets elsewhere in the same component. I lowered the score from 87 to 83 to reflect this miss, but the overall verdict (solid craft, ship-ready, ship with minor fixes) survives.

refutation.note:
All three reviewer defects verified directly against index.html CSS and the full-res postsave.png crop, and hold up:
1. .btn--ghost (Undo) confirmed transparent background/border (lines 156-160) — zoomed crop of the toast confirms zero button chrome, Undo distinguished from "Change saved" only by weight/color, and from the X icon only by weight. Hover/focus states do exist in code (line 161-162 hover, line 136-137 focus-visible outline in accent) but are correctly noted as "not visible in the static frame" — an accurate caveat, not a false claim.
2. --color-accent (#ed4609) confirmed defined (line 18) and confirmed absent from .btn--ghost's resting color (var(--color-fg-muted) at line 158) — accent only ever appears in the shared :focus-visible outline, not as a resting CTA signal. Claim holds.
3. Both .snackbar__message (line 222) and .btn/.snackbar__undo (line 122, inherited) use var(--type-body, 16px) — confirmed literally identical via grep. Claim holds exactly as measured.

I additionally computed contrast for Undo (#b8b8b8) against the snackbar's --color-bg-elev (#141414): ~8:1, well past AA — so this is not a contrast defect, just an affordance/hierarchy one, consistent with how the reviewer framed it (they never claimed a contrast failure).

One defect the reviewer missed: the 5-second auto-dismiss timer (AUTO_DISMISS_MS = 5000, line 307) has no pause-on-hover/focus — I grepped for mouseenter/mouseleave/focusin/focusout and found none; clearTimeout only fires on explicit Undo/Dismiss click (line 324). Combined with Undo's weak affordance, a user who is slow to notice/read the toast has no way to extend the window before Undo disappears — a real WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable) gap, medium severity. This compounds the reviewer's three low-severity nits rather than contradicting them.

Net: verdict sustained, ship-ready stands (nothing here blocks shipping a low-stakes demo harness), but the true defect count is 4, not 3, so I docked a few points off the original 85.

refutation.note:
All three defects verified directly against the artifact and hold up.

High (button wrap): Confirmed by pixel-measuring both idle.png and postsave.png — cropped the action row and the "Save change" label visibly wraps to "Save"/"change" on two lines in BOTH captures, giving the button roughly 2x its single-line height. Root cause matches the reviewer's read exactly: `.btn` (line 128-140) has no `white-space:nowrap` or `flex-shrink:0`, and `.demo-actions` (line 121-125) is a plain flex row sharing the 480px `.demo` max-width with a long hint string — default flex-shrink lets the button shrink below max-content width before the hint string gives up any space, so the button wraps. This is a real, visible defect in a build otherwise praised for restraint, and it appears in both judged screenshots — high severity is justified.

Medium (Undo vs message weight/color): Verified byte-for-byte — `.snackbar-message` (line 208-213) is 16px/default-weight/white, `.btn-undo` (line 224-235) is 16px/500-weight/`--accent` #ed4609. Same size confirmed, so the reviewer's core measurement claim (equal type scale, differentiated only by weight+color) is accurate. Whether bold saturated-orange "outweighs" plain white is a legitimate but somewhat subjective visual read — I'd call it defensible rather than open-and-shut, but the underlying evidence is correct and the code comment context (accent reserved for the interactive control) makes this a real tension worth flagging, not a fabricated one.

Low (hint text wrap): Confirmed in both screenshots — hint wraps after "the" in idle.png and after "or" in postsave.png, inside the same cramped `.demo-actions` row. Real, low severity as scored.

No defects overturned. I did not find additional high/medium defects the reviewer missed on top of these three — the snackbar component itself (tokens, undo/dismiss/timer, aria-live+role=status, focus-visible, Escape handling) checks out against the code exactly as the reviewer described in strengths.

refutation.note: All three reviewer-cited defects check out against the CSS: message and Undo are both var(--type-body)=16px/font-weight:500 (index.html lines 22, 146, 204-211, 282-283 — .btn--text never overrides size/weight, confirmed by reading the full ruleset); .snackbar__actions gap is var(--space-xs)=4px (lines 35, 293); dismiss glyph is a 16x16 viewBox, stroke-width 1.5 (lines 401-404). I independently recomputed the accent-on-bg-elev contrast via WCAG relative-luminance formula (Python, not eyeballed): #ed4609 on #141414 = 4.81:1, matching the reviewer's ~4.7:1 claim and clearing AA — my first manual pass mis-parsed the hex (read G as 0x40 instead of 0x46) and got a false 4.3:1 fail; the script confirms the reviewer's number, not my error, so this strength claim survives too. Screenshots match the code: idle.png shows the snackbar genuinely absent from the DOM (matches region.innerHTML='' / no persistent hidden node), postsave.png shows the described divider + color-only hierarchy. One thing the reviewer didn't surface: onUndoPressed sets state=UNDOING and reverts fieldValue after a 250ms setTimeout, but simulateOptimisticSave's re-entry guard only checks `state !== STATE.HIDDEN` to clear the auto-dismiss timer — it doesn't branch on UNDOING, so a Save press during that 250ms window could capture previousValue before the pending revert completes, producing an inconsistent revert history. This isn't visible in either static screenshot and would need interactive fuzzing to confirm, so I'm reporting it as unverified-by-screenshot rather than a confirmed defect — it wouldn't move the score materially either way. No claim in the reviewer's report was contradicted by the artifact; the verdict and score stand.

refutation.note:
Verified against index.html and both renders. All three reviewer-cited line ranges (.snackbar__message ~251-258, .snackbar__undo ~267-280) check out: message has no explicit font-weight, Undo is 500-weight accent orange, both inherit --type-body:16px — the core proportion claim (single flat 16px size, hierarchy via color/weight not size) is accurate and confirmed visually in postsave.png. The ellipsis-truncation defect (#3) is also accurate — no title/aria-label fallback exists on .snackbar__message.

Defect #2 (dismiss-icon contrast) is OVERTURNED on its own math: I computed the actual contrast of --color-fg-dim #828282 on --color-bg-card #1c1c1c using the standard WCAG relative-luminance formula and got ~4.43:1, not the reviewer's claimed ~3.9:1 — a comfortable 47% margin above the 3:1 non-text floor, not 'the thinnest margin of any color pairing in the component' as claimed.

That framing also pointed at the wrong element. Computing the SAME formula for the actual accent orange (#ed4609) against the same card background gives ~4.45:1 — nearly identical margin to the dismiss icon, so the icon isn't uniquely marginal at all. More importantly, that 4.45:1 number is the Undo button's own text-on-background contrast, and it's the PRIMARY interactive control of the component. WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal-weight text under 18pt/14pt-bold (500-weight doesn't qualify as 'bold' for the large-text exemption), so Undo's own label color sits just under the AA text threshold — a real, if marginal, accessibility miss the reviewer didn't catch because they were looking at the dismiss X instead of the element that actually carries the risk.
